CAUSE CONFIRMED (red-team, reproduced with the real functions): the probe_warmup cache key excludes the arm flags, so all four arms share the blob minted by T0P0 (use_noise_floor=False, always the cache MISS); _restore_cached_surface object.__setattr__s the mint arm's root attribute surface onto each cache-HIT agent, overwriting the live NoiseFloor instance with the mint arm's None, after which the guarded call site (agent.py:3444) is skipped and no lift is ever computed. Do NOT record substrate_ceiling from this run: MECH-063 already carries 3 prior substrate_ceiling autopsy hits under the R1-R3 convention, and this is a harness-wiring fault, not a ceiling.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: probe_warmup cache restore overwrites arm-conditional regulators with the mint arm's None
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: The warmup cache key (_warmup_key) excludes the arm's runtime flags, so one blob is shared across a 2x2 whose arms construct DIFFERENT root-level regulators. _restore_cached_surface then object.__setattr__s the mint arm's surface onto every HIT agent, silently replacing a live arm-conditional regulator (agent.noise_floor, constructed only when use_noise_floor=True) with the mint arm's None. Nothing raises and nothing logs it: assert_state_dict_shareable passes because these regulators are zero-parameter and non-nn.Module, and the restore's missing-module logging only covers cached paths ABSENT here, never the reverse. Fix options: include arm-conditional flags in the cache key; or exclude arm-constructed regulator attributes from the restored surface; or have the driver reinstall ALL arm regulators post-warmup rather than only phasic_burst. Add an assertion that every arm-conditional regulator is non-None after restore when its flag is set.

Cause: cache-restore overwrites agent.noise_floor with the mint arm's None; _fresh_regulator reinstalls only phasic_burst, so phasic survived (R_transient non-zero 10/10 PHASIC-ON) and tonic did not.

arguments_withdrawn.argument: Sampling starvation (16/20 cells hit the step cap at ~60% of target selections) explains the collapsed effect.
arguments_withdrawn.withdrawn_because: REFUTED by the 779a comparison. 779a met its sample floors on 3/20 cells (step_cap 15, episode_cap 2); this run on 4/20 (step_cap 16). Starvation is essentially IDENTICAL across the two runs, yet mean_dS_tonic differs 50-fold (0.2654 vs 0.0053). Starvation is real and worth fixing, but it is not the discriminating variable. The manifest's own sampling_shortfall block already warns against routing on it.

arguments_withdrawn.argument: The SD-074 warmup cache fails to restore the NoiseFloor regulator's warmed state, leaving the tonic axis cold and unable to lift.
arguments_withdrawn.withdrawn_because: REFUTED by code read. NoiseFloor is documented 'stateless across ticks' and compute_effective_temperature computes lifted = baseline + alpha unconditionally, with no dependence on _n_waking_calls or any accumulated state. A cold regulator lifts identically to a warmed one. NOTE the underlying blind spot is nonetheless REAL and worth reporting separately: NoiseFloor is zero-parameter and non-nn.Module, so it is invisible BOTH to assert_state_dict_shareable (which checks state_dict key/shape parity, and whose docstring cites exactly this zero-parameter property as what licenses cache sharing) AND to _restore_cached_surface (which walks agent.named_modules()). It is simply not the cause of this failure.
arguments_withdrawn.withdrawal_CORRECTED_after_red_team: This withdrawal was RIGHT IN ITS REASONING BUT STOPPED ONE STEP SHORT, and the conclusion it drew was wrong. Correct: NoiseFloor is stateless with respect to the lift, so a COLD regulator lifts identically to a warmed one -- restoring warmed state was never the issue. Missed: the restore does not leave the regulator COLD, it overwrites it with NONE (the mint arm T0P0 has use_noise_floor=False, so its captured root surface carries noise_floor=None). So the warmup machinery IS the cause after all, by a different mechanism than the one withdrawn. The blind-spot observation recorded here was therefore not merely 'real but not the cause' -- it was adjacent to the actual cause and should have prompted a check of WHAT the restore writes, not only whether the regulator needs warmed state.

arguments_withdrawn.argument: noise_floor_alpha is configured to 0.0, so the lift is trivially zero.
arguments_withdrawn.withdrawn_because: REFUTED: config records tonic_noise_floor.alpha = 1.0. Notably 779a's measured lift_mean was exactly 1.0 == alpha, confirming the regulator fired on every tick there and on zero ticks here.

learning_extracted: The decisive move on this run was comparing against the predecessor's per-cell instrument reading, not its headline result. noise_floor_temp_lift_mean 1.0 -> 0.0 identified an inert manipulation immediately, where the headline (mean_dS_tonic 0.265 -> 0.005) alone would have read as a weak or negative result.

A matched confound is a free control. 779a and 963 are almost equally sample-starved, which converts starvation from a candidate explanation into a held-constant nuisance variable and refutes it in one line.

RECORDING GAP: NoiseFloor.get_state() already exposes n_waking_calls and last_n_simulation_skips, which together separate 'regulator never called' from 'called under simulation_mode'. Neither was recorded, so a re-run is currently needed to answer a question the substrate was already computing.

The baseline_entropy_headroom precondition passed (met=True) while ALL FOUR arms appear in saturating_arms with worst_margin 0.0037 against a warn_margin of 0.15. The gate tests membership of the band [0.02, 0.98], not the margin to its edge, so it admits a run with effectively no headroom.
A capability precondition evaluated on a worst-cell basis (tonic_axis_live) correctly refused this run. That gate worked; it is the reason the manifest's evidence_direction is already right.

A withdrawal can be locally valid and still wrong: 'NoiseFloor is stateless, so a cold regulator lifts identically' is TRUE and refutes the stated hypothesis, yet the real fault was in the same machinery -- the restore writes None over the live regulator. When withdrawing a hypothesis about a mechanism, check what the mechanism WRITES, not only whether the target needs the state it fails to carry.

The asymmetry was the discriminating evidence and was sitting in the cells the whole time: phasic live (R_transient non-zero on 10/10 PHASIC-ON cells), tonic dead (lift 0.0 on all 20). Only a cause that distinguishes the two regulators explains it -- and _fresh_regulator reinstalls exactly one of them. Look for the asymmetry a hypothesis must explain before enumerating hypotheses.
